## Research

- **SpineFairBench** (Co-author, with Ahmed Taha and Muzzammil Ahmadzada):Paired counterfactual evaluation suite for auditing demographic sensitivity in spinal-radiology vision-language model (VLM) reports. Evaluates a frozen nine-model VLM panel across 7,996 source/counterfactual pairs (apparent age and sex edited under target-pathology preservation). Recommendation drift observed in all nine models; 443/450 stratified pairs (98.4%) passed blinded review by three board-certified radiologists. Paper: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/404620116 · Code: https://github.com/ahmedtaha100/SpineFairBench · Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ahmedtaha100/spinefairbench-artifacts
- **MedInsider: A Benchmark for Documentation Integrity in Medical LLM Agents Under Institutional Pressure** (Co-author, with Ahmed Taha and Muzzammil Ahmadzada): LLM-agent evaluation suite spanning 840 clinical scenarios (420 matched pairs), 5 regulatory failure families, and 8 incentive conditions, measuring whether medical LLM agents preserve decision integrity under institutional and financial pressure. Engineered deterministic simulated-EHR tooling, action logging, audit pipelines, and scoring across a 9-model evaluation panel. Paper: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/405798471_MedInsider_A_Benchmark_for_Documentation_Integrity_in_Medical_LLM_Agents_Under_Institutional_Pressure

## Selected Projects

- **APEX — Arrhythmia Pattern Explainer**: End-to-end ECG decision-support system classifying 71 diagnostic categories at 0.920 macro-AUROC on PTB-XL, served via FastAPI at 6 ms inference. Reliability layer with per-lead Grad-CAM grounding and four consistency/confidence checks; reduced Expected Calibration Error from 0.079 to 0.002 (97%) via per-label vector scaling, cutting spurious findings 93%. https://github.com/abdeltaehass/apex-arrhythmia-explainer
- **SENTRY — Vision-Language Incident Report Generator**: LoRA-adapted vision-language reporting pipeline shipped as a production FastAPI service with Docker, API-key authentication, rate limiting, GitHub Actions CI/CD, and 143 passing tests. Evaluated 10,000 manually reviewed outputs and reduced ungrounded claims 35%. https://github.com/abdeltaehass/SENTRY
- **S.A.I.N.T. — Network Intrusion Detection System**: AI agent reasoning engine reaching 89% accuracy on NSL-KDD (125K+ samples). 41 traffic-flow features classified in real time; Flask + Redis + Plotly low-latency inference at 50–100 connections/sec with an interactive agent-in-the-loop dashboard. https://github.com/abdeltaehass/S.A.I.N.T.
- **StockPulse — Autonomous Stock & Crypto Monitoring Platform**: Full-stack autonomous trading monitor integrating Alpaca (equities) and Binance (crypto) with real-time crash detection, ML-based price prediction, and unified portfolio tracking. Multi-agent alert pipeline with Telegram notifications, 24/7 surveillance, Docker-containerized. https://github.com/abdeltaehass/stockpulse
- **PingVault — Network Observability Agent**: Production-grade network monitoring across ICMP, SNMP, TCP/UDP with agent-based metrics collection, Alembic migrations, and a real-time HTML observability dashboard. https://github.com/abdeltaehass/PingVault
- **AutoApply**: Full-stack job-application toolkit. Scrapes CalCareers (and external boards), calls the Claude API to generate tailored resumes, cover letters, and SOQs per posting, scores fit on a 0–100 scale. https://github.com/abdeltaehass/AutoApply
- **GovCon**: Web platform for government contractors to track contracts, deadlines, and documentation. https://abdeltaehass.pythonanywhere.com/bids
- **Al-Manar (Production iOS App)**: Shipped to the App Store with Flutter/Dart, owning the full lifecycle from UI/UX through automated distribution via Xcode Cloud CI/CD. Custom background audio framework extending BaseAudioHandler with system-level media controls and optimized memory handling; Google Places API + Haversine geospatial calculations for GPS-accurate prayer times, localized across 9 languages. https://apps.apple.com/us/app/al-manar/id6759625182

## Open Source Contributions

- **Google MCP Security** (merged, PR #283, Aug 2026 · Python): MCP Security is Google's toolkit that lets AI assistants query Chronicle, its security operations platform. A function that fetched detections for a security rule passed its arguments in the wrong order, so a filter like “only alerting detections” landed in a date field and crashed the request; corrected the call, exposed the time-range options it had been hiding, and added regression tests. https://github.com/google/mcp-security/pull/283
- **Google gVisor** (merged, PR #14144, Aug 2026 · Go): gVisor is Google's sandbox for safely running untrusted code, used in Google Cloud. Developers installing it as a Go library kept hitting a confusing build error; tracked down the cause and documented the correct install path in the README and setup guide. https://github.com/google/gvisor/pull/14144
- **Google gVisor** (approved, PR #14395, Sep 2026 · Go / C++): Overwriting a program’s file while that program was still running quietly corrupted the running image and usually killed it with a bus error. Real Linux refuses the write outright; gVisor tracked nothing of the kind. Added a count of the processes currently executing a file, held for exactly as long as the kernel holds its own, and taught the three filesystems that can host executables to reject writes and truncations before the file is touched. Verified against native Linux and five gVisor configurations, including checkpoint/restore. https://github.com/google/gvisor/pull/14395
- **NVIDIA CCCL** (merged, PR #10790, Aug 2026 · CUDA C++ / Python): CCCL is NVIDIA's core CUDA library, used by GPU developers worldwide. Debuggers showed almost no useful detail when inspecting GPU memory objects; rewrote that display logic and added tests covering 12 scenarios against real GDB and LLDB output. https://github.com/NVIDIA/cccl/pull/10790
- **NVIDIA CCCL** (merged, PR #10881, Aug 2026 · CUDA C++): A memory-saving optimization in NVIDIA's CUDA headers was written with syntax some compilers ignore, so it quietly did nothing on those platforms. Replaced it with the library's own portable macro so it applies everywhere. https://github.com/NVIDIA/cccl/pull/10881
- **NVIDIA CCCL** (merged, PR #11059, Sep 2026 · CUDA C++): Including a Thrust header without a CUDA compiler produced roughly 1,300 unrelated errors, none of which named the actual cause. Added a check that reports the real problem in one line and names the ways out, placed so it fires before the downstream noise begins. Review narrowed it further, so a host-only build still compiles as long as the CUDA toolkit headers are present. https://github.com/NVIDIA/cccl/pull/11059
- **Uber NullAway** (merged, PR #1694, Aug 2026 · Java): NullAway is Uber's tool that catches null-pointer crashes in Java before code ships. Its tests pulled sample code from scattered files; moved that code inline next to the tests that use it and deleted the obsolete files, keeping coverage identical. https://github.com/uber/NullAway/pull/1694
- **Uber NullAway** (merged, PR #1712, Aug 2026 · Java): Follow-up applying the same cleanup to NullAway's largest test file, covering its Android, RxJava, Java Streams, and Lombok support. Brought 8 fixture files' worth of sample code inline so each test reads on its own, without changing what the suite verifies. https://github.com/uber/NullAway/pull/1712
- **Uber NullAway** (merged, PR #1765, Sep 2026 · Java): The third and largest file in the same cleanup. Beyond moving the sample code inline, one shared fixture could not simply be deleted: other test classes were quietly compiling it off the classpath by name, so removing it broke twelve of their tests. At the maintainer's suggestion, hoisted it into a shared constants class and pointed every consumer at it, which let the fixture directory be deleted entirely. https://github.com/uber/NullAway/pull/1765
- **Uber NullAway** (merged, PR #1832, Sep 2026 · Java): NullAway cached its dataflow analysis in the Java compiler's shared context, so whichever run reached it first decided the configuration every later run inherited. Moved it onto the checker instance itself, created on first use, matching how the tool already holds the rest of its per-compilation state. The maintainer added a compile-time guard on top so the object can no longer be built the wrong way. https://github.com/uber/NullAway/pull/1832
- **Elastic EUI** (merged, PR #9913, Aug 2026 · TypeScript / React): EUI is Elastic's design system, used throughout Kibana. Modernized the date picker's quick-select control from an older React pattern to current hooks, keeping its public API, behavior, and appearance identical. https://github.com/elastic/eui/pull/9913
- **Elastic EUI** (merged, PR #9971, Sep 2026 · TypeScript / React): A second EUI migration, this one with a wrinkle: the data grid's column-resize handle attaches its drag listeners to the browser window on mouse down, and the very same functions have to be there to unhook them on release. Moved it to hooks while preserving that, added cleanup on unmount, and rewrote the tests to drive real mouse events rather than calling the component's methods directly. https://github.com/elastic/eui/pull/9971
